messages:
Ravi: Quick sketch: propose a hybrid 'sliding-window envelope' admission that combines a short token-bucket for spikes + a slow-decaying baseline (EMA). Goal: limit sustained overshoot while allowing short bursts. Thoughts? :thought_balloon:

Mira: Sounds useful. How many state fields per tenant? We want tiny footprint for millions of tenants.

Ravi: Plan: store baseline_rate (float), fast_bucket_level (int), last_ts. That's 3 fields. Fast bucket refills with short interval, baseline updates via EMA.\n
Chen: Interface question: priority/reserved tenants — do we special-case? We should let the priority layer request envelope boosts via a capability flag rather than bypass. Keeps signal boundaries clean.

Sam: Rollout: dual-run mode with tenant hash gating (old || new). Start 2% canary, watch rejection delta and p99 latency. ops-bot, annotate the canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary: sliding-envelope v1 -> 2% tenants at 2026-03-25T11:00Z. Monitoring enabled. :rocket:

Mira: Telemetry needs: per-tenant baseline, fast_level, rejections_fast/rejections_slow. Aggregate: %tenants in slow-reject > 5m. Also export a fairness score (Gini of allowed rate).

Ravi: API stub:
```
Admission.Check(tenant, api_key, tokens, priority, client_hint) -> {admit:bool, reason:str, bucket_state:str}
```

Chen: Edge: many short-lived client_ids can amplify burst. Recommend canonicalizing by api_key and a small per-client deduction so one client doesn't consume entire burst. Also cap concurrency.

Sam: Testing: synthetic workload generator with steady, sawtooth spikes, and fanout short-lifers. Compare against reservoir baseline for fairness and memory CPU.

Mira: I'll craft dashboards and alert thresholds. Suggest alert if >0.1% tenants hit slow-mode for >10m.

Ravi: Action items: 1) I'll write RFC with math + migration plan. 2) @Chen build canonicalization + per-client deduction prototype. 3) @Mira dashboards. 4) @Sam test harness + rollout playbook. Review RFC by Fri.
